newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senate says Speaker stops bill-drafters work.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senate says Speaker stops bill-drafters work.

text.p: The New York State Senate Marjority Leader on Wednesday, predicting a difficult session, charged the Assembly Speaker with stopping bills from being drafted in a fight over $56,000 of stipends for members.

Republican Gov. George Pataki at a special legislative session in December declined to approve the stipends, called "lulus," for seven members of the Assembly, which is led by Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan.
"Shelly (Silver) said he wants his stipends and he wants them done now," said Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, who is the Senate Leader. "The speaker has closed down bill drafting,"

The Senate Majority Leader told reporters in Albany that the Assembly Leader was holding up the nomination of Ron Backer, the new Republican co-chair of the bill drafting commission, a bipartisan group, and the pay checks of its 200 staffers.
The bills can still be printed by other entities, however.

Pataki, a Republican, did not approve the stipends for the Assembly members because Silver did not sign a bill for a $12 billion capital program, which includes funds for an upstate prison, for the Metropolitan Transportation Agency, by an agreed deadline, Bruno told reporters.

The Leader added Pataki's stand on the stipends also was due to the Speaker's rejection of an energy tax bill for ratepayers, which Silver turned down as he feared it would reward shareholders, Bruno told reporters.
A spokeswoman for Pataki had no response immediately available.

Silver, in prepared remarks, appeared to try to take the high road, saying "The Senate Majority Leader's comments this afternoon are most unfortunate." He also faulted Bruno for going back on what Silver said was a promise to conduct "the business of the legislature with dignity and civility."

Bruno held out little hope that the state, which last year set a national record for late budgets, would find the process much easier this year. "I believe this will be the most contentious session we have had in government in a lot of years, and it's going to be because Speaker Silver is refusing to recognize that the campaigns are over and it's time for us in this state to get on with governing," he said.
